First, let's list out the user stories again to map to activities:
U1: Friendly name for chaincode
U2: Lifecycle system chaincode for deployment policies
U3: Documentation for upgrade flows
U4: Solo ordering process (single orderer, in-memory ledger, seek support, disconnection/reconnection)
U5: Public GitHub repo for Fabric code
U6: State cache for rw-set building
U7: Centralized Fabric docs on hyperledger.org
U8: Separate CLI tool for Fabric components, extracted from peer, no RocksDB dependency for the CLI

1. For U4 (Solo orderer): Use a single-threaded consumer for the buffered channel, in-memory ledger with append-only log and seek API, support client offset tracking for reconnection.
2. For U8 (CLI tool): Decouple CLI command logic from peer node internal dependencies, use Go modules to separate the CLI package, build platform-specific binaries without RocksDB linkage for the CLI.
3. For U6 (State cache): Implement a read-through LRU cache for world state, invalidate entries on chaincode commit, expose cache API for rw-set generation.
4. For U2 (Lifecycle SCC): Extend existing lifecycle system chaincode with new deployment policy management functions (define, query, update policies) with access control.
5. For U1 (Chaincode friendly name): Add a name field to chaincode definition metadata, update chaincode registration and query APIs to support friendly name lookup.
6. For U5 (Public GitHub): Mirror existing Gerrit-hosted Fabric repo to public GitHub, set up CI/CD for public repo to sync with main Gerrit changes.
7. For U7 (Docs): Consolidate all Hyperledger project docs into a single Docusaurus instance hosted on hyperledger.org, add navigation for Fabric-specific docs.
8. For U3 (Upgrade flow docs): Write step-by-step documentation for chaincode upgrade, including policy requirements, rollback procedures, and sample commands.

Now assumptions. Let's list reasonable ones:
1. All development uses existing Hyperledger Fabric codebase as the starting point, no need to build core Fabric from scratch.
2. For U4 (Solo orderer), the existing orderer codebase is used as a reference, and the Solo implementation is a lightweight alternative to Kafka/Raft consensus.
3. The public GitHub repo (U5) will be a read-only mirror of the main Gerrit repository, with no separate development workflow required.
4. The state cache (U6) will use existing world state storage interfaces, no changes to underlying state database required.

8. Testing for all components will use existing Fabric test frameworks, no new test infrastructure needs to be built.

1. Activity ID: A1, Name: Implement chaincode friendly name feature (U1). Description: Add friendly name field to chaincode metadata, update chaincode registration, query, and listing APIs to support friendly name lookup, add validation for unique friendly names per channel. Effort: 3 workdays. That makes sense, it's a metadata addition, API updates, validation.

2. Activity ID: A2, Name: Extend lifecycle system chaincode for deployment policy management (U2). Description: Add new lifecycle SCC functions to define, query, and update chaincode deployment policies, implement access control for policy management functions, add policy validation logic. Effort: 5 workdays. Because it's extending SCC, adding functions, access control, validation, that's a bit more work.

3. Activity ID: A3, Name: Write upgrade flow documentation (U3). Description: Create step-by-step documentation for chaincode upgrade process, including policy requirements, pre-upgrade checks, upgrade execution steps, rollback procedures, and sample CLI commands. Effort: 2 workdays. Documentation, based on existing docs, so 2 days is reasonable.

5. Activity ID: A5, Name: Set up public GitHub mirror for Fabric codebase (U5). Description: Configure read-only mirror of main Gerrit-hosted Fabric repository to public GitHub, set up CI/CD pipeline to sync changes from Gerrit to GitHub, add contribution guidelines and issue templates for public repo. Effort: 2 workdays. Mirror setup, CI sync, templates, 2 days.

6. Activity ID: A6, Name: Implement state cache for rw-set generation (U6). Description: Implement read-through LRU cache for world state, add cache invalidation logic on chaincode commit/update, expose cache API for rw-set builder to use, add unit tests for cache hit/miss and invalidation scenarios. Effort: 6 workdays. LRU cache, invalidation, API exposure, tests, that's 6 days.

7. Activity ID: A7, Name: Consolidate Hyperledger documentation on hyperledger.org (U7). Description: Set up centralized Docusaurus documentation site on hyperledger.org, migrate existing Fabric and other Hyperledger project docs to the new site, add cross-project navigation and search functionality. Effort: 4 workdays. Site setup, migration, navigation, 4 days.

8. Activity ID: A8, Name: Develop standalone Fabric CLI tool (U8). Description: Extract peer CLI commands into separate Go module, decouple command logic from peer node internal dependencies and RocksDB, implement platform-specific binary build pipelines for Mac and Windows, add basic integration tests for CLI commands. Effort: 7 workdays. Extracting commands, decoupling, build pipelines, tests, 7 days.
